title: Automorphic Residues Count Squarefree Divisors — and the Product-of-Local-Rings Mechanism
description: The parent entry proves that ZMod n has exactly 2^ω(n) idempotents (equivalently, 2^ω(n) automorphic residues e²≡e mod n), where ω(n) is the number of distinct primes dividing n. This entry answers the parent's first open question — how does that count generalize beyond ℤ? — from two directions. Arithmetically, 2^ω(n) is exactly the number of squarefree divisors of n: the map s ↦ ∏ p∈s p is a bijection from the powerset of n's prime factors onto the squarefree divisors, so the automorphic residues of n are equinumerous with its squarefree divisors (idempotents_eq_squarefreeDivisors). Algebraically — the direction the open question actually asks for — the count is a power of two because the Chinese Remainder Theorem writes the modulus as a finite product of LOCAL rings, and a local ring has no idempotents besides 0 and 1. This entry isolates that mechanism for an arbitrary commutative ring: idempotent_count_pi_local shows a finite product of nontrivial local rings ∏ᵢ Rᵢ has exactly 2^(number of factors) idempotents, and idempotent_count_of_ringEquiv transports the count across any ring isomorphism S ≃+* ∏ᵢ Rᵢ. For ZMod n the local factors are the ZMod(pᵢ^eᵢ), recovering 2^ω(n); for the quotient 𝒪_K/𝔞 of a number ring by an ideal — the object named in the open question — the local factors are the 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵢ^eᵢ, giving 2^(number of distinct prime ideals dividing 𝔞). The local-ring fact isIdempotentElem_iff_eq_zero_or_one_of_isLocalRing does the essential work: for idempotent e, e·(1−e)=0, and in a local ring one of e, 1−e is a unit, forcing its partner to vanish.

mainTheorems.name: idempotent_count_of_ringEquiv
mainTheorems.statement: (φ : S ≃+* ∀ i, R i) → [each Rᵢ a nontrivial local ring, ι finite] → Nat.card {e : S // IsIdempotentElem e} = 2 ^ Nat.card ι
mainTheorems.description: The idempotent count of any commutative ring isomorphic to a finite product of nontrivial local rings is 2^(number of factors). This is the general form of the open question: the Chinese Remainder Theorem supplies such an isomorphism for ZMod n and for 𝒪_K/𝔞, so both counts are powers of two governed by the number of local factors.
mainTheorems.significance: Answers the parent's open question at the level of mechanism, not just for ℤ: the count is 2^(number of local CRT factors), whether those factors are ZMod(pᵏ) or 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵏ.

mainTheorems.name: idempotent_count_pi_local
mainTheorems.statement: [each Rᵢ a nontrivial local ring, ι finite] → Nat.card {e : (∀ i, R i) // IsIdempotentElem e} = 2 ^ Nat.card ι
mainTheorems.description: A finite product of nontrivial local rings has exactly 2^(number of factors) idempotents. Each local factor contributes its two idempotents 0 and 1 independently, and idempotents of a product are exactly the coordinatewise idempotents.
mainTheorems.significance: The ring-theoretic heart of every 2^ω-style idempotent count: the power of two comes from an independent binary choice at each local factor.

mainTheorems.name: idempotents_eq_squarefreeDivisors
mainTheorems.statement: 0 < n → Nat.card {e : ZMod n // e * e = e} = (squarefreeDivisors n).card
mainTheorems.description: The automorphic residues of n — the idempotents of ZMod n — are equinumerous with the squarefree divisors of n. Both counts equal 2^ω(n).
mainTheorems.significance: Gives the parent's abstract count 2^ω(n) a concrete divisor-theoretic meaning: each idempotent corresponds to a choice of squarefree 'support' divisor built from a subset of n's primes.

mainTheorems.name: isIdempotentElem_iff_eq_zero_or_one_of_isLocalRing
mainTheorems.description: A local ring has no idempotents besides 0 and 1. For idempotent e we have e·(1−e)=0; in a local ring one of e, 1−e is a unit, and a unit annihilating its partner forces that partner to be 0.
mainTheorems.significance: The single fact that makes each local factor contribute exactly 2 idempotents; without it the CRT decomposition would not yield a power of two.

mainTheorems.name: squarefreeDivisors_card
mainTheorems.description: The number of squarefree divisors of n is 2^ω(n), via the bijection s ↦ ∏ p∈s p from the powerset of n.primeFactors onto the squarefree divisors (Finset.card_image_of_injOn + Finset.card_powerset).
mainTheorems.significance: The arithmetic side of the count: squarefree divisors are indexed by subsets of the prime-factor set, so there are 2^ω(n) of them.

mainTheorems.name: idempotent_count_local
mainTheorems.statement: [IsLocalRing R] [Nontrivial R] → Nat.card {e : R // IsIdempotentElem e} = 2
mainTheorems.description: A nontrivial local ring has exactly two idempotents. Packages the {0,1} characterization as an equivalence with Bool.
mainTheorems.significance: The per-factor base case: 2 = 2^1, the building block of the product count.

sections.title: Overview: Automorphic Residues Count Squarefree Divisors
sections.summary: Imports (Mathlib + parent AutomorphicNumberOQ01OQ01) and module docstring. The grandparent shows ZMod (10^k) has exactly four idempotents; the parent explains 'four' as 2^ω(n), the number of automorphic residues e²≡e (mod n). This file gives that count two further meanings. Arithmetic shadow: 2^ω(n) equals the number of squarefree divisors of n (squarefreeDivisors_card), and idempotents of ZMod n are equinumerous with them (idempotents_eq_squarefreeDivisors), via the bijection with the powerset of n.primeFactors. Algebraic mechanism: for arbitrary commutative rings, a finite product of nontrivial local rings has exactly 2^(#factors) idempotents (idempotent_count_pi_local, idempotent_count_of_ringEquiv) — a local ring has only 0,1 as idempotents and product idempotents are tuples. Via CRT this recovers 2^ω(n) for ZMod n and generalizes to 𝒪_K/𝔞 = 2^(#distinct prime ideals). 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
sections.mathContext: The open question motivating the entry is how 2^ω(n) generalizes beyond ℤ; the local-product idempotent count is the ring-theoretic mechanism, answering it for number-field quotients 𝒪_K/𝔞 through the CRT decomposition into local factors.

sections.title: Part I: Squarefree divisors and the powerset bijection
sections.summary: squarefreeDivisors n := {d ∈ n.divisors | Squarefree d}. prod_mem_squarefreeDivisors: a product ∏ p∈s p over a subset s of n's prime factors is a squarefree divisor (divisibility via Nat.prod_primeFactors_dvd; squarefreeness because distinct primes are pairwise coprime). squarefreeDivisors_eq_image: every squarefree divisor is recovered as ∏ over its own prime factors, so the squarefree divisors are exactly the image of n.primeFactors.powerset under s ↦ ∏ p∈s p. injOn_prod_powerset: that map is injective on the powerset since primeFactors is a left inverse on sets of primes (Nat.primeFactors_prod).
sections.mathContext: Squarefree divisors of n ⟷ subsets of the prime-factor set of n, via the product-of-a-subset-of-primes bijection.

sections.title: Part II: The count 2^ω(n) and the bridge to automorphic residues
sections.summary: squarefreeDivisors_card: card_image_of_injOn on the bijection plus Finset.card_powerset gives #squarefree divisors = 2^ω(n). idempotents_eq_squarefreeDivisors: composing with the parent's idempotent_count shows the automorphic residues of n are equinumerous with its squarefree divisors. Corollaries pin the degenerate cases: count = 1 ⟺ n = 1, count = 2 ⟺ n is a prime power, and the decimal recovery #squarefreeDivisors(10^k) = 4.
sections.mathContext: #{idempotents of ZMod n} = #{squarefree divisors of n} = 2^ω(n); the classical decimal '4' is the case ω(10^k)=2.

sections.title: Part III: Local rings have only the trivial idempotents
sections.summary: isIdempotentElem_iff_eq_zero_or_one_of_isLocalRing: a local ring has only the idempotents 0 and 1. For idempotent e, e·(1−e)=0; IsLocalRing.isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self makes one of e, 1−e a unit, and IsUnit.mul_right_eq_zero forces its partner to vanish (no NoZeroDivisors needed — a local ring like ZMod pᵏ can have zero divisors). idempotent_count_local packages this as a cardinality fact: the idempotent subtype is equivalent to the two-element set {0,1}, so Nat.card_coe_set_eq and Set.ncard_pair give exactly 2.
sections.mathContext: This is the single local fact every later count leans on: e·(1−e)=0 plus 'one of e, 1−e is a unit' pins e to {0,1}, with no assumption that R is a domain.

sections.title: Part IV: The product-of-local-rings mechanism and transport (the open question)
sections.summary: isIdempotentElem_pi_iff: idempotents of a product ring are exactly the coordinatewise idempotents. idempotent_count_pi_local: subtypeEquivRight and subtypePiEquivPi give {idempotents of ∏ Rᵢ} ≃ ∀ i, {idempotents of Rᵢ}, so Nat.card_pi turns the count into a product of 2 over the factors, i.e. 2^(card ι) — this is the theorem that directly answers the open question's generalization request. idempotent_count_of_ringEquiv transports the count across any ring isomorphism S ≃+* ∏ Rᵢ (idempotents correspond under a ring iso via map_mul and injectivity), the form applicable to ZMod n and 𝒪_K/𝔞 via CRT.
sections.mathContext: The count is 2^(number of local factors) because each local factor of the CRT decomposition contributes an independent binary idempotent choice, and that count is invariant under any ring isomorphism onto the product.

overview.historicalContext: The idempotents of a finite commutative ring, and their count as a power of two, are a classical consequence of the structure theory of Artinian rings: every such ring is a finite product of local rings, and a local (indeed any connected) ring has only the trivial idempotents 0 and 1. For ℤ/nℤ this product decomposition is exactly the Chinese Remainder Theorem, ℤ/nℤ ≅ ∏ ℤ/pᵢ^{eᵢ}ℤ, so the number of idempotents is 2^{ω(n)} — the decimal shadow of which is the recreational fact that there are two nontrivial k-digit automorphic numbers for every k. The same decomposition holds for the ring of integers 𝒪_K of a number field modulo an ideal 𝔞: unique factorization of ideals gives 𝔞 = ∏ 𝔭ᵢ^{eᵢ}, and CRT yields 𝒪_K/𝔞 ≅ ∏ 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵢ^{eᵢ} with each factor local, so the idempotent count is 2^{(number of distinct primes dividing 𝔞)}. This entry formalizes the ring-theoretic mechanism behind all of these counts — a finite product of local rings has 2^{(number of factors)} idempotents — together with the arithmetic reinterpretation of the ℤ-case count as the number of squarefree divisors.
overview.problemStatement: The parent entry proves #{idempotents of ℤ/nℤ} = 2^{ω(n)} and asks how the count generalizes beyond ℤ, e.g. to 𝒪_K/𝔞. Two questions are addressed: (1) arithmetic — identify 2^{ω(n)} concretely as the number of squarefree divisors of n; (2) algebraic — isolate, for an arbitrary commutative ring, the mechanism that makes the count a power of two, in a form that applies to any ring the Chinese Remainder Theorem writes as a finite product of local rings (both ℤ/nℤ and 𝒪_K/𝔞).
overview.proofStrategy: For the arithmetic side, exhibit the bijection s ↦ ∏_{p∈s} p from the powerset of n.primeFactors onto the squarefree divisors of n: a product of a subset of the distinct primes is a squarefree divisor (divisibility from Nat.prod_primeFactors_dvd, squarefreeness because distinct primes are pairwise coprime), every squarefree divisor is the product over its own prime factors, and the map is injective because primeFactors is a left inverse on sets of primes. Finset.card_image_of_injOn and Finset.card_powerset then give 2^{ω(n)}, and composing with the parent's idempotent_count bridges to automorphic residues. For the algebraic side, first prove a local ring has only the idempotents 0 and 1: for idempotent e, e·(1−e)=0, and IsLocalRing.isUnit_or_isUnit_one_sub_self makes one of e, 1−e a unit, which annihilating its partner forces the partner to 0. The idempotent subtype is then the two-element set {0,1} (0≠1 in a nontrivial ring), of cardinality 2. Idempotents of a product ring are the coordinatewise idempotents (isIdempotentElem_pi_iff), so subtypePiEquivPi give an equivalence {idempotents of ∏ Rᵢ} ≃ (∀ i, {idempotents of Rᵢ}), whence Nat.card_pi yields the product of 2 over the factors, i.e. 2^{(card ι)}. Finally, idempotents transport across a ring isomorphism (Equiv.subtypeEquiv with the predicate correspondence IsIdempotentElem e ↔ IsIdempotentElem (φ e), from map_mul and injectivity), giving the count for any S ≃+* ∏ Rᵢ.
keyInsights: The power of two in every 2^ω-style idempotent count comes from a single ring-theoretic fact: a local ring has no idempotents besides 0 and 1, so each local factor of a CRT decomposition contributes an independent binary choice.
The essential local-ring argument is one line of algebra: for idempotent e, e·(1−e)=0, and since one of e, 1−e is a unit in a local ring, its partner must vanish — so e ∈ {0,1}.
Idempotents of a finite product ring are exactly the tuples of idempotents of the factors; there is no interaction between factors, which is why the counts multiply to a pure power of two.
The count 2^{ω(n)} for ℤ/nℤ has a concrete divisor-theoretic face: it is the number of squarefree divisors of n, indexed by subsets of the prime-factor set via s ↦ ∏_{p∈s} p.

Phrasing the general statement through a ring isomorphism S ≃+* ∏ Rᵢ makes it directly applicable to 𝒪_K/𝔞: the Chinese Remainder Theorem provides the isomorphism, the local factors are 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵢ^{eᵢ}, and the count is 2^{(number of distinct prime ideals dividing 𝔞)} — the answer the open question conjectured.

Using Nat.card throughout (rather than Fintype.card) keeps the local factors and the ambient ring free of finiteness hypotheses beyond the finite index set of factors, so the mechanism theorem is stated at full generality.

conclusion.summary: The idempotent count 2^{ω(n)} of the parent entry is given two further meanings. Arithmetically it is the number of squarefree divisors of n, via the bijection between subsets of n's prime factors and squarefree divisors. Algebraically it is a special case of a general mechanism: a finite product of nontrivial local rings ∏ᵢ Rᵢ has exactly 2^{(number of factors)} idempotents (each local factor contributes its two idempotents 0 and 1 independently), and this count transports across any ring isomorphism S ≃+* ∏ᵢ Rᵢ. The Chinese Remainder Theorem supplies such an isomorphism for ℤ/nℤ (local factors ℤ/pᵢ^{eᵢ}ℤ) and for 𝒪_K/𝔞 (local factors 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵢ^{eᵢ}), so both idempotent counts are powers of two governed by the number of distinct primes. Fully machine-checked: 0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide.
conclusion.implications: The entry explains why every CRT-driven count of idempotents is a power of two, and does so at the level of arbitrary commutative rings rather than ℤ specifically. The general theorems idempotent_count_pi_local and idempotent_count_of_ringEquiv apply verbatim to the number-field setting named in the open question: given the CRT isomorphism 𝒪_K/𝔞 ≅ ∏ 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵢ^{eᵢ} (each factor local) the idempotent count is 2^{(number of distinct prime ideals dividing 𝔞)}. The squarefree-divisor reinterpretation connects the count to standard multiplicative number theory (the divisor function 2^{ω} = number of squarefree divisors).
openQuestions: Can the CRT isomorphism 𝒪_K/𝔞 ≅ ∏ 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵢ^{eᵢ} be produced in Mathlib and fed to idempotent_count_of_ringEquiv to state the number-field count 2^{(number of distinct prime ideals dividing 𝔞)} as a standalone theorem, including the fact that each 𝒪_K/𝔭ᵢ^{eᵢ} is a local ring?

For a general finite commutative ring, the idempotents biject with the clopen subsets of Spec(R), giving 2^{(number of connected components)}; can idempotent_count_pi_local be upgraded to this topological form via the primitive-idempotent decomposition, removing the explicit product hypothesis?

crossReferences.description: Counting Automorphic Residues mod n as 2^ω(n) — proves the count this entry reinterprets (as squarefree divisors) and generalizes (as the product-of-local-rings mechanism); its idempotent_count is reused directly in the bridge theorem.
The Complementary Pairing of Automorphic Idempotents — studies the involution e ↦ 1−e on the idempotents that this entry counts; the pairing reflects the two idempotents 0 and 1 of each local factor.

Chinese Remainder Theorem (Constructive) — the source of the ring isomorphism S ≃+* ∏ Rᵢ into local factors that idempotent_count_of_ringEquiv consumes; the mechanism behind both the ℤ/nℤ and 𝒪_K/𝔞 counts.

Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic — unique factorization underlies both ω(n) and the squarefree-divisor bijection, and (in its ideal-theoretic form) the CRT decomposition of 𝒪_K/𝔞 into prime-power local factors.
